title: Segmented event-log and idempotent replay for tenant chargeback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: The current billing pipeline performs best-effort ingestion and downstream joins which complicate deterministic attribution and makes backfills lengthy and error-prone. We lack an immutable, segmentable trail that supports partial reprocessing and exact-once semantics for tenant chargeback windows. Goal: introduce a segmented event-log (append-only) for token usage events, design an idempotent replay mechanism with replay watermarking and compaction policies, and wire a deterministic aggregator that produces stable per-tenant chargeables for billing exports. Deliverables: (1) event-log schema and write path, (2) idempotent replay worker + watermark store, (3) deterministic windowed aggregator that uses replay markers, (4) backfill/replay tooling and runbook, (5) dashboards and alerts for drift/regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Event-log accepts enriched usage events (session_id, request_id, tenant_id, model_id, token_counts, seq_ts) with <=100ms median write latency under 2k rps ingest
Replay worker can reprocess a tenant's segment from arbitrary watermark T and produce identical aggregation output when run twice (idempotent), verified by checksum equality
Backfill tool can replay a 30-day window for a single tenant and complete within the operational SLA for on-demand replays (target: 6 hours), with progress markers persisted
Chargeback export contains stable per-tenant chargeable rows (token counts, model route, price tier) and matches live-run for non-replayed windows within 0.1% tolerance
Rollout includes feature flag gating and automatic fallback to legacy aggregator if critical errors are detected
End-to-end observability: latency + error SLOs, per-tenant replay lag metric, and drift alert when reprocessed vs. live output diverge >0.5%
design_notes: We model the event-log as time-partitioned segments keyed by tenant_id + day, written to an append-only store (S3/Parquet or Kafka compacted topic). Each event carries deterministic sequence metadata to allow ordering and rerun determinism.

Idempotency: worker computes a stable output signature per aggregation window (SHA256 of sorted output rows) and writes watermark entries (tenant, window_end, signature, version). Replays compare signatures to decide no-op vs. emit updated rows.
Compaction policy: after 90 days, segments are compacted to weekly aggregates to reduce storage and replay time; compaction writes match the same signature scheme.

Watermark store: small low-latency DB (Cockroach or Dynamo) to track per-tenant per-window watermarks and last_replay_id. Access frequency is low but requires transactional updates to avoid concurrency anomalies.
Compatibility: aggregator will accept both legacy raw input and new event-log; a compatibility shim will translate older event shapes during rollout.

Trade-offs: Kafka provides lower-latency streaming but complicates long-term replay storage; S3-parquet provides cheap immutable archival and faster bulk backfills. Initial implementation will use a hybrid: streaming to Kafka for nearline + daily dumps to S3 for durable replays.
implementation_plan: Schema PR: open PR with event schema, ingestion contract, and sample producer/consumer (owner: @migue) — 2d
Ingest path: add producer instrumentation in runtime gateway to emit enriched events (owner: @asha) — 5d
Event-log storage: prototype dual-write to Kafka + S3 daily segments, ensure exactly-once producer semantics — 5d
Replay worker: implement idempotent replay worker that reads S3 segments by tenant+window and writes aggregation outputs and watermark updates (owner: @migue) — 7d
Aggregator: build deterministic windowed aggregator that uses watermark store and emits stable charge rows into billing staging table — 6d
Backfill tooling: CLI to schedule replays with concurrency limits, progress markers, and automatic retries — 3d
E2E tests: golden-run tests that replay the same segment twice and assert signature equality and stable exports — 4d
PR/Code review and docs: design doc in Confluence, runbook in Ops, and GitHub PRs — 3d
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): enable event dual-write for 5 beta tenants; run aggregator in dry-run mode and compare outputs to legacy pipeline for 48 hours
Phase 1 (Staged): enable aggregator for low-volume tenants (10% of accounts) with feature flag; keep legacy pipeline as fallback; monitor drift metrics
Phase 2 (Bulk): allow on-demand backfills for enterprise customers and start compaction jobs for 90-day windows
Phase 3 (Cutover): switch billing exports to the new aggregator for new invoices once drift tolerance maintained for 7 days; keep a read-only archive of legacy invoices for audits
Fallback: feature flag to route exports back to legacy aggregator, with automated safety checks to prevent double-billing
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboard: per-tenant drift heatmap comparing legacy vs new aggregator by month
SLOs: event ingestion availability 99.9%, replay completion SLA for on-demand backfills 6 hours
risk_mitigation: Keep legacy exporter as golden copy for fallbacks and audits
Run deterministic golden tests in CI that validate signatures for synthetic and sampled real traffic
Limit initial dual-write to a small cohort to reduce blast radius
Design watermark updates to be transactional to prevent double-processing on worker restarts
Perform cost analysis for S3 storage vs Kafka retention before bulk enablement
runbook_and_docs: Ops runbook: how to trigger on-demand replay, monitor progress, abort gracefully
Developer guide: event schema, producer libraries, and backfill CLI examples
